evidence.reason: nothing is inferred and nothing is run: each home is a row of synthetic days drawn from distributions written down here

inference.label: online filter
inference.provenance: declared by the experiment that wrote the record

metric_definitions.abstention_rate: Fraction of estimates that declined to name a state, because confidence or sensor coverage fell below threshold.
metric_definitions.accuracy: Fraction of scored estimates whose reported state equals the true state. A reported UNKNOWN is never correct, so abstentions count as errors.
metric_definitions.balanced_accuracy: Unweighted mean of per-class recall. Used in preference to accuracy because the states are heavily imbalanced and a model that always predicts the majority state scores highly on raw accuracy.
metric_definitions.brier: Multiclass Brier score over the full posterior, in [0, 2]. A proper scoring rule; lower is better.
metric_definitions.calibration_error: Expected calibration error: the bin-weighted gap between stated confidence and observed accuracy. Answers whether a confidence of 0.9 means anything.
metric_definitions.ci_low, ci_high: Bootstrap confidence interval on the mean paired difference. Reported instead of a p-value: with simulations, significance is a statement about how long the computer ran.
metric_definitions.confusion: Counts of labelled true state (rows) against reported state (columns). The final column is UNKNOWN, so abstentions stay visible.
metric_definitions.contaminated_fraction: Fraction of simulated time during which someone other than the monitored resident was present.
metric_definitions.detected_changes: Number of true changes detected across the seeds in an arm, which is the sample size behind median_delay_days.
metric_definitions.effect_size: Cohen's dz for the paired difference. Note that pairing removes between-household variance, so dz is larger than an unpaired field study of the same size would produce.
metric_definitions.f1: Harmonic mean of precision and recall.
metric_definitions.false_positives_per_person_day: Delivered alerts not matched to a true change, divided by monitored person-days. The alert burden a recipient experiences.
metric_definitions.log_loss: Mean negative log probability assigned to the true state. Punishes confident errors far more than hedged ones.
metric_definitions.macro_f1: Unweighted mean F1 across the classes present in the truth.
metric_definitions.mean_difference: Mean paired difference between two configurations evaluated on identical simulated trajectories.
metric_definitions.mean_seed_median_delay_days: Mean across seeds of each seed's own median delay. Reported alongside median_delay_days because it weights every seed equally regardless of how many changes it detected; it is not a median.
metric_definitions.median_delay_days: Median days between a true change occurring and an alert being delivered for it. A detection counts only if it falls at or after the change and within max_delay_days. Where an arm aggregates several seeds, the individual delays are pooled before taking the median, so this is a median over detections and not a mean of per-seed medians.
metric_definitions.per_class_recall: Recall for each state present in the ground truth.
metric_definitions.precision: True positives divided by predicted positives.
metric_definitions.recall: True positives divided by actual positives.
metric_definitions.selective_accuracy: Accuracy among only the estimates that committed to a state. Read together with abstention_rate.

notes: Synthetic data only. Nothing here reads TIHM or runs the pipeline, so nothing here is evidence about a home.
Made before the sleep-mat protocol was frozen, to choose its interval and to say how often each criterion's readings come out when the truth is known.
1,000 synthetic studies in each scenario, each with a generator derived from one recorded root. docs/SIMULATION_PROTOCOLS.md sets a floor of 100.
Each study resamples its homes 2,000 times for the bootstrap, fewer than a protocol would.

results.rule: the interval whose lowest coverage over every scenario is the higher is chosen
